findings.issue: The `restock_events` table's dedup key is `["inventory_item_external_id", "inventory_updated_at"]` and the trigger's `idempotency` field states "if a restock_event already exists for the same inventory item and the same updated_at timestamp" — but `inventory_updated_at` (or any `updated_at` equivalent) is absent from the trigger's `signalFields` list and has no corresponding `payloadBinding`. The coding agent has no declared source for this value and will either fabricate it, use `NOW()` (which breaks idempotency entirely since two deliveries of the same event would produce different timestamps), or omit the column. The dedup guarantee — the plan's entire guard against double-enqueuing notifications — collapses silently.
findings.fix: Add `"inventory updated at"` to the trigger's `signalFields` and add a payloadBinding `{signalField: "inventory updated at", source: "payload", payloadPath: "updated_at"}` so the coding agent reads the real webhook timestamp; then surface it in `record-restock-event`'s `dataNeeds` so it is threaded into the INSERT.

findings.issue: `item_availability_states` declares `statusField: "availability_status"` which the spec requires to be paired with at least one write capability that has `usesWorkflow: true` (binding the `workflow` helper for atomic claim/complete/fail lifecycle). `record-restock-event` is the only capability that writes to this table and transitions `availability_status` (its description says "update the item's last-observed availability state"), yet it declares `usesWorkflow: false`. Without the flag the coding agent will hand-roll an UPDATE instead of using the atomic workflow helper, creating an inventory-race window where two concurrent webhook deliveries both pass the transition check before either commits.
findings.fix: Set `usesWorkflow: true` on `record-restock-event`; the `workflow` helper's atomic claim-then-complete pattern is exactly the concurrency guard needed when two `inventory_levels/update` deliveries race on the same `inventory_item_external_id`.

findings.issue: `send-restock-email` declares `"item page url"` in its `dataNeeds`, but no plan element supplies this value: the `inventory_levels/update` payload bindings carry no URL, no upstream Shopify step fetches a product handle or online-store URL, and `notification_queue` stores no URL column. The coding agent has no described source and will either invent a URL construction scheme or silently omit the link from the email — breaking the core click-through path that drives the "lost demand recovered" metric.
findings.fix: Either (a) add a `product_handle` column to `notification_queue` (populated at enqueue time from the `detect-restock` Shopify step which already produces product metadata) and list `"product handle"` in `send-restock-email`'s `dataNeeds`, or (b) add a resolution note to the `detect-restock` shopifySteps entry stating that `onlineStoreUrl` or handle is captured and threaded through `record-restock-event` into `notification_queue`.
